purpose: Verify that report references and report details remain readable without weakening tenant isolation.

items.title: Internal service can open a completed report from another tenant scope
preconditions: A persisted evaluation exists under tenant scope tenant-a.
The caller is authenticated with the matching.service role.
steps: Call GET /api/v1/evaluations/{evaluation_id} with the service credential.
Use a service access scope that differs from tenant-a.
items.expected: HTTP 200 returns the persisted evaluation and its task metadata.

items.title: Tenant user cannot open a report from another tenant scope
preconditions: A persisted evaluation exists under tenant-a.
The caller is authenticated as a normal tenant identity for tenant-b.
steps: Do not set the internal service-wide flag.
items.expected: The result is not disclosed and the API returns the stable not-found response.

items.title: Internal service receives not-found for an unknown report ID
preconditions: The caller is authenticated with the matching.service role.
items.expected: HTTP 404 with EVALUATION_NOT_FOUND; no unrelated evaluation is returned.
items.automation: Add route-level regression coverage for the service-wide branch.

items.title: Report list entries are detail-readable
preconditions: GET /matches/reports returns at least one reference with evaluation_id.
steps: Load the Evidence Court report selector.
items.expected: Every selectable entry either opens a report or is explicitly marked unavailable; no raw MATCHING_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND error is shown.
items.automation: Add an end-to-end test covering list-to-detail consistency.

items.title: Pending references are not presented as completed evidence reports
preconditions: The report list contains a pending reference without evaluation_id.
steps: Inspect the pending entry and its enabled state.
items.expected: Pending work is either hidden from the completed-report selector or shown as disabled with a clear processing status.
items.automation: Add an EvidenceCourt component test for pending and failed references.

items.title: A stale but readable report still renders its evidence
preconditions: A persisted evaluation is readable and marked stale.
steps: Open the report in Evidence Court.
Inspect the verdict banner and evidence sections.
items.expected: The report renders, visibly explains the stale reason, and offers recomputation guidance without hiding the evidence.
items.automation: Add a component test with stale=true and stale_reason_codes.

items.title: Evidence Court keeps requirement context while deduplicating evidence
preconditions: The same evidence result_reference supports two distinct requirements.
steps: Build evidence groups from the evaluation report.
Inspect the rendered rows and their requirement references.
items.expected: The UI does not lose the requirement-to-evidence relationship when deduplicating repeated evidence.
items.automation: Extend groupEvaluationEvidence.test.ts with repeated evidence across requirements.

items.title: Report display labels do not depend on the current user’s private lists
preconditions: A reviewer can read a report belonging to another user.
The reviewer cannot list the owner’s private resume.
steps: Open the Evidence Court selector as a reviewer.
Inspect the report label and subject metadata.
items.expected: The selector receives an authorized display label from the API or uses an intentional masked label; it does not degrade to missing-name text without explanation.
items.automation: Add a contract test for reviewer-visible report metadata.
